title: IdentityProviderConnection

$schema.description: Editor affordance: path or URL of this schema so editors validate and autocomplete the file (scaffolded connection files point at `.zitadel/meta/idp-connection.json`). Ignored by the platform.

slug.x-zitadel-pattern-message: must start with a lowercase letter or digit and use only lowercase letters, digits, _ and -
slug.description: Stable identifier of the identity provider. User schemas (`x-auth-methods.sso.providers`) and flow steps (`sso_providers`) reference it. Unique within the project.

protocol.description: The protocol used by the identity provider. OIDC is the only protocol.

template.description: A hint for rendering the provider (logo, colors). It carries no protocol behavior: behavior comes only from the protocol blocks.

display_name.description: Shown to the user on the sign-in button.

subject_claim.description: The claim (a named piece of user data the provider returns) that carries the provider's stable subject identifier. Optional; the server uses `sub`, as the OIDC specification defines. Override it where `sub` is pairwise, for example Entra `oid`.

claim_mapping.description: Maps user schema property names (keys) to provider claim names (values). A value is an exact top-level claim key: no path syntax, and a dot is part of the key, so nested claims (OIDC `address`) are not addressable yet. `$`-prefixed strings and non-string values are reserved for future mapping forms. Add properties defined in the user schemas; unmatched entries are ignored.

verified_claims.description: Maps a verifiable user schema property to its verification source: a claim name (read the claim) or the literal `true` (trust this provider unconditionally). Values starting with `$` are reserved for future sources. Distinct from `claim_mapping`, which carries values, not verification state.

provisioning.description: How far this provider's data is trusted. `creation` defines what happens to a subject that has no account yet. With `disabled`, a user is not created. With `auto`, the user is created without a collection step (the step that asks the user for missing data) when the mapped claims fill every required property of the schema. A required property with an `x-unique` scope must also arrive verified according to `verified_claims`. When a required property is missing or such a property is unverified, the collection step is shown instead, prefilled with the claims. Gating on other properties is not available yet. These are not available yet either: the `auto_only` value, which creates the user from complete claims or fails without collecting; the linking policy (`is_linking_allowed`, `auto_linking`), together with the account-linking journey; and `is_auto_update`, together with per-property verification state.

oidc.description: OIDC settings of the identity provider. Endpoints come from the issuer's discovery document (its `.well-known` document). A provider that exposes no `.well-known` document names them all instead: `authorization_endpoint`, `token_endpoint`, `jwks_uri`, and `userinfo_endpoint` unless `id_token_mapping` is set. Setting any endpoint without the others is rejected with `idp.endpoints_partial`; set all of them or none.

issuer.x-zitadel-pattern-message: must be an https URL (http is allowed for localhost only)
issuer.description: Discovery base. Endpoints are resolved from its `.well-known` document unless the document names them all.

jwks_uri.x-zitadel-pattern-message: must be an https URL (http is allowed for localhost only)
jwks_uri.description: JWKS endpoint, for a provider that exposes no .well-known document. Set together with the other endpoints.

id_token_mapping.description: Read user claims from the id_token instead of the userinfo endpoint, for providers that populate only the former.

authorization_endpoint.x-zitadel-pattern-message: must be an https URL (http is allowed for localhost only)
authorization_endpoint.description: For a provider that exposes no .well-known document. Set together with the other endpoints.

token_endpoint.x-zitadel-pattern-message: must be an https URL (http is allowed for localhost only)
token_endpoint.description: For a provider that exposes no .well-known document. Set together with the other endpoints.

userinfo_endpoint.x-zitadel-pattern-message: must be an https URL (http is allowed for localhost only)
userinfo_endpoint.description: For a provider that exposes no .well-known document. Set together with the other endpoints; not needed when id_token_mapping is set.

client_id.description: Either a literal, when all environments use the same client, or a `${{ NAME }}` reference to a variable, when each environment has its own client.

client_secret.x-zitadel-pattern-message: must be a variable reference such as ${{ CLIENT_SECRET }}, not the secret itself
client_secret.description: A reference to the variable holding the client secret, never the secret itself. A secret may only be referenced as the entire value: text around the placeholder would be rendered into the resolved credential, so it is rejected. The server resolves it against the environment serving the request.

token_endpoint_auth_method.description: How the client authenticates at the token endpoint.

scopes.description: Must contain `openid`: without it the provider returns no id_token and the sign-in is not OIDC. An omitted `scopes` is rejected. The default (`openid`, `profile`, `email`) only pre-fills editors; validators never inject it.

pkce_enabled.description: Send PKCE (`code_challenge` and `code_verifier`), which binds the code exchange to the client that started it. Providers that do not support PKCE typically ignore the parameters, so `true` is safe and future-proofs; set `false` only for a provider whose token endpoint rejects them.

static_authorize_parameters.description: Extra provider-specific authorize parameters (for example `prompt`). Protocol parameters the server sets are reserved and rejected by `propertyNames`: the server composes them itself, and an override of `state` or `nonce` would silently defeat CSRF and token binding. `client_secret` and `client_assertion` are rejected as they could be appended to the public authorize URL.
